_about: Hand-written plain-language summaries of common CWE weaknesses. Names follow MITRE; text is paraphrased, never copied. Source of truth: https://cwe.mitre.org.

entries.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
entries.plain: Untrusted input can add or change properties on JavaScript's shared object prototype, so every object in the process inherits them.
entries.impact: Can change application logic, bypass checks, crash the process or, in some code paths, lead to code execution.
entries.matters_when: The app merges, clones or sets nested keys from request bodies, query strings or JSON it does not control.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; reject keys like __proto__, constructor and prototype; use Object.create(null) or Map for untrusted keys.

entries.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
entries.plain: Some input makes the code use far more CPU, memory or other resources than it should, without a limit.
entries.impact: Denial of service: the process slows down or stops responding for everyone.
entries.matters_when: Attackers can reach the affected code with input they choose, for example through a public endpoint.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; cap input sizes and request rates; add timeouts.

entries.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
entries.plain: A regular expression can take exponential time on specially crafted strings (ReDoS).
entries.impact: One request can pin a CPU core for seconds or minutes, blocking a single-threaded server.
entries.matters_when: The vulnerable pattern runs on input a user controls, such as headers, URLs or form fields.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; limit input length before matching; avoid nested quantifiers.

entries.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
entries.plain: Input ends up inside code that the program builds and runs, so an attacker can make it run their own code.
entries.impact: Arbitrary code execution with the application's permissions.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted data reaches the affected function, for example templates, expressions or eval-like features.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; never pass untrusted input to code generation or eval.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
entries.plain: User-supplied text is placed into a web page without proper escaping, so a browser runs it as script.
entries.impact: Attackers can act as the victim in the browser: steal sessions, read data or change what the page does.
entries.matters_when: The affected code renders HTML that includes data from users or other untrusted sources.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; escape output by context; use a Content-Security-Policy.

entries.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
entries.plain: The code allocates memory, connections or other resources for each request without a cap.
entries.impact: Denial of service by exhausting memory or connections.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted clients can trigger the allocation repeatedly or with large inputs.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; set size, count and rate limits.

entries.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
entries.plain: An attacker can make the server send requests to addresses of their choosing, including internal ones.
entries.impact: Access to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints that should not be reachable from outside.
entries.matters_when: The affected client fetches URLs or hosts derived from user input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; allow-list destinations; block private and link-local addresses.

entries.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
entries.plain: Information that should stay private is revealed to someone who should not see it.
entries.impact: Leaked credentials, personal data or internal details that help further attacks.
entries.matters_when: The affected code handles secrets, cookies, headers or personal data.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; review what is logged, returned or forwarded.

entries.name: Improper Input Validation
entries.plain: Input is not checked well enough before it is used.
entries.impact: Depends on where the input goes: crashes, wrong behaviour or a path to other attacks.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted data reaches the affected function.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; validate type, length and format at the boundary.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Windows Device Names
entries.plain: File names like CON, NUL or COM1 are treated as normal files on Windows when they are really devices.
entries.impact: Hangs, crashes or unexpected file access on Windows hosts.
entries.matters_when: The app runs on Windows and builds file paths from user input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; reject reserved device names in user-supplied paths.

entries.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
entries.plain: Code treats a value as one type when it is really another, for example an array where a string was expected.
entries.impact: Checks can be bypassed or the process can crash or misbehave.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted input (such as parsed query strings or JSON) can change a value's type.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; check types explicitly before use.

entries.name: Uncontrolled Recursion
entries.plain: Deeply nested input makes a function call itself until the stack runs out.
entries.impact: Crash or denial of service.
entries.matters_when: Attackers can send deeply nested data (JSON, query strings, markup) to the affected parser.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; limit nesting depth.

entries.name: Improper Authentication
entries.plain: The code does not properly prove who a user or client is.
entries.impact: Attackers may act as other users or reach protected functions.
entries.matters_when: The affected package is part of login, token or session handling.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; review authentication flows and token checks.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
entries.plain: Data is passed to another component (shell, query, header, template) without escaping its special characters.
entries.impact: The downstream component may run commands or change meaning in ways the attacker controls.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted input flows through the affected code into another interpreter.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; use parameterised APIs and context-aware escaping.

entries.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
entries.plain: The app redirects users to a URL taken from input without checking where it points.
entries.impact: Phishing: links on your domain can send users to an attacker's site.
entries.matters_when: Redirect targets come from query parameters or other user input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; allow only relative paths or known hosts.

entries.name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
entries.plain: Output is not encoded correctly for where it is used, so special characters change its meaning.
entries.impact: Can enable injection or corrupted output in the receiving component.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted data is written into HTML, headers, URLs, logs or other structured formats.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; encode for the exact output context.

entries.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
entries.plain: The code accepts data without properly checking that it really comes from the expected source.
entries.impact: Forged or tampered data can be trusted.
entries.matters_when: The affected code verifies signatures, tokens or upstream responses.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; verify signatures and origins strictly.

entries.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
entries.plain: Another site can make a logged-in user's browser send requests the user did not intend.
entries.impact: Actions performed as the victim, such as changing settings or data.
entries.matters_when: The app uses cookie-based sessions and state-changing requests.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; use CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
entries.plain: A small compressed input expands into a huge amount of data when unpacked.
entries.impact: Memory or disk exhaustion (a 'zip bomb').
entries.matters_when: The app decompresses uploads, archives or compressed request bodies.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; cap decompressed size and ratio.

entries.name: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary ('Confused Deputy')
entries.plain: The component forwards requests on behalf of an attacker, lending them its access.
entries.impact: Attackers reach systems or actions that should only be available to the component.
entries.matters_when: The affected code proxies requests or follows redirects for clients.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; restrict what can be forwarded and where.

entries.name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
entries.plain: The code does not handle rare or error conditions correctly.
entries.impact: Crashes, hangs or security checks skipped under unusual input.
entries.matters_when: Attackers can trigger the unusual condition, for example with malformed input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version.

entries.name: Path Traversal: 'dir/../../filename'
entries.plain: Sequences like ../ in a path let input escape the intended directory.
entries.impact: Reading or writing files outside the allowed folder.
entries.matters_when: File paths are built from user input or archive entries.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; resolve paths and check they stay inside the base directory.

entries.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
entries.plain: Input can point a file operation outside the directory it is meant to be limited to.
entries.impact: Reading or overwriting arbitrary files the process can access.
entries.matters_when: File paths come from requests, archive entries or other untrusted sources.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; normalise paths and enforce a base directory.

entries.name: Relative Path Traversal
entries.plain: Relative path segments in input reach files outside the intended directory.
entries.impact: Reading or writing files outside the allowed folder.
entries.matters_when: Paths are built from user input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; reject '..' segments after normalising.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting')
entries.plain: Line breaks in input end up in HTTP headers, letting an attacker add headers or split responses.
entries.impact: Cache poisoning, session fixation or cross-site scripting via injected responses.
entries.matters_when: Header values are built from user input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; strip CR and LF from header values.

entries.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
entries.plain: The code relies on a cryptographic algorithm or mode that is known to be weak.
entries.impact: Encrypted or signed data may be read or forged.
entries.matters_when: The affected code protects secrets, tokens or integrity checks.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; use current, recommended algorithms.

entries.name: Protection Mechanism Failure
entries.plain: A security protection is missing, disabled or can be bypassed.
entries.impact: The attack the protection was meant to stop becomes possible.
entries.matters_when: Your app relies on the affected protection (for example a sanitiser or security header).
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version.

entries.name: Out-of-bounds Write
entries.plain: Code writes past the end (or before the start) of a buffer.
entries.impact: Memory corruption: crashes or, in native code, possible code execution.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted data reaches the affected native or low-level code.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version.

entries.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
entries.plain: The app turns untrusted bytes back into objects with a format that can trigger code during loading.
entries.impact: Often arbitrary code execution.
entries.matters_when: Serialized data comes from users, files or network peers you do not control.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; use safe formats like JSON for untrusted data.

entries.name: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
entries.plain: Sensitive data is included in data sent to another party, such as headers forwarded on redirects.
entries.impact: Credentials or cookies leak to a third party.
entries.matters_when: The affected client sends authenticated requests or follows redirects across hosts.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; avoid forwarding credentials across origins.

entries.name: Permissive List of Allowed Inputs
entries.plain: An allow-list accepts more values than it should.
entries.impact: Inputs that should be rejected get through and can enable other attacks.
entries.matters_when: Your app relies on the affected validation for security decisions.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; tighten allow-lists.

entries.name: Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)
entries.plain: A cheap request causes expensive work on the server.
entries.impact: Denial of service with little effort from the attacker.
entries.matters_when: The affected code path is reachable by untrusted clients.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; add limits and rate limiting.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
entries.plain: Input is placed into an SQL query in a way that can change the query itself.
entries.impact: Reading, changing or deleting database data; sometimes more.
entries.matters_when: Untrusted input reaches the affected query builder.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; use parameterised queries.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
entries.plain: Input is passed to a shell command so it can add commands of its own.
entries.impact: Arbitrary commands run on the server.
entries.matters_when: The affected code builds shell commands from untrusted input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; avoid the shell and pass arguments as a list.

entries.name: Embedded Malicious Code
entries.plain: The package contains code written to do harm, such as stealing secrets or opening a backdoor.
entries.impact: Anything the package can reach when installed or imported, including credentials on that machine.
entries.matters_when: The package was installed anywhere: developer machines, CI or production.
entries.mitigation: Remove the package, reinstall from a clean lockfile and rotate secrets on affected machines.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Unsafe Equivalence in Input
entries.plain: Inputs that look different but are treated as equal (for example by case or encoding) slip past checks.
entries.impact: Validation or access rules can be bypassed.
entries.matters_when: The affected code compares names, paths or identifiers from untrusted input.
entries.mitigation: Upgrade to a fixed version; normalise input before comparing.
